faqs.question: What is a tax refund advance?
faqs.answer: A refund advance lets eligible taxpayers receive a portion of their refund before the IRS finishes processing. Tax Fighters offers Holiday Advances (no fee) and Shield Advances ($500–$7,500). You can always refuse an advance and wait for the full IRS refund.

faqs.question: How quickly can I receive a tax refund advance?
faqs.answer: Depending on the product and your file, you may receive funds in about 30 minutes or within 24–48 hours after we complete your return and the bank approves the advance.

faqs.question: What happens if my tax refund is less than the advance amount?
faqs.answer: Advances are sized from the completed return. The advance and any bank fees are deducted from the IRS refund when it posts. We review the numbers with you before you accept funds.

faqs.question: What is the cost associated with a tax refund advance?
faqs.answer: The Tax Fighters does not charge fees on Holiday Advances. Shield Advances may include bank fees that depend on the amount. Fees are disclosed in full before we process, and they come out of the final refund — not a separate payment.

faqs.question: Can I refuse an advance if I am not interested?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. You can decline every advance and wait for the entire refund. Preparers respect that choice.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Photo ID, SSN, W-2s or pay stubs, children’s birth certificates and SSNs, and proof each dependent lived with you for at least six months. We may request more documents to finish an accurate return.

blogPosts.title: A guide for income tax preparation & advances
blogPosts.excerpt: What Holiday and Shield Advances are, what to bring, and how repayment works when the IRS pays.
blogPosts.body:
Tax refund advances are short-term funds against a completed return. Holiday Advances carry no Tax Fighters fee. Shield Advances range from $500 to $7,500 and may include bank fees.

Bring ID, SSNs, W-2s or pay stubs, and dependent documents. After we file, approved clients can take an advance. The IRS refund later repays the advance and any disclosed fees automatically.

You can always say no and wait for the full refund.
blogPosts.author: E. Bel

blogPosts.title: Information about referral program and bonuses
blogPosts.excerpt: How existing clients earn when family and friends file with The Tax Fighters.
blogPosts.body:
Tell your people to mention your name at intake. After their return is filed, you receive the posted referral bonus. There is no charge to the person you send.

Ask your preparer for this season’s amount. Bonuses are one of the ways we thank clients who keep the waiting room full.
blogPosts.author: The Tax Fighters Team

blogPosts.title: How to find the right business tax preparation & audit support
blogPosts.excerpt: Schedule C and 1120 filings, plus a safety net if the IRS writes. Existing clients are not charged for audit support.
blogPosts.body:
Gather income statements, expenses, and receipts. Use the right form — Schedule C for sole proprietors, 1120 for corporations — and bring it to the preparer.

We file for the business and stay on the file if an audit starts. Existing Tax Fighters clients are not charged for audit support. That is the safety net.
